chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilya al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the Talbiyah of al-Mut'ah (Hajj al-Tamattu'), when is it cut off? He said: When one enters the Haram (sanctuary of Mecca). The correct approach in this narration is to consider it permissible (mubah), while the earlier one is for excellence and recommendation, so that the reports do not contradict each other.

key_terms.الْمُتْعَة: Al-Mut'ah (a type of Hajj involving temporary pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim stop reciting the Talbiyah during Hajj al-Mut'ah?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, the termination of Talbiyah during Hajj al-Mut'ah is linked to entering the Haram, a ruling that Shaykh al-Tusi reconciles with other reports by distinguishing between the permissibility of delaying the cut-off and the superior merit of doing so earlier. This approach reflects the Shia principle of *jam'* (reconciliation) between seemingly contradictory hadiths, prioritizing the recommended (*mustahabb*) nature of early termination while maintaining the validity of the later timing. The context highlights the nuanced juristic methodology in al-Isfabar regarding the ritual precision of Hajj rites.
